blocks.text: On the night of 5 to 6 May, people all over Turkey celebrate *Hıdırellez* (also written *Hıdrellez*), the festival of spring and of the summer to come. Its name joins two figures of folk belief. *Hızır* is said to have drunk the water of life, so that he never dies; he wanders the earth, especially in spring, helping people in trouble, and stands for new life. *İlyas* is the prophet Elijah. According to tradition, the two meet on earth on this night.

In the old folk calendar, the day opens the summer half of the year: the 186 *Hızır günleri*, the days of Hızır, run from 6 May to 8 November, and the 179 *Kasım günleri*, the days of November, make up the winter.

Before the festival, houses are cleaned from top to bottom so that Hızır will want to visit, and people buy new clothes. On the day itself families go out to green places near water for a picnic, often with lamb on the menu, and in many towns a fire is lit in the evening: jumping over it three times is said to keep illness away for the year.

Wishes are at the heart of the night. People write them on paper, or draw or make a small model of what they hope for, such as a house or a garden, and hang it on the branches of a rose bush or bury it at its foot. In the morning the wishes are collected and, by custom, given to running water. Some leave a coin under the rose bush and keep it in their wallet all year as *bereket parası*, money for plenty.

An older custom is a game of fortune, played mostly by young women. Each one drops a ring, an earring or another small object into a pot of water, which is covered and left under a rose bush overnight. The next day the objects are drawn out one by one while someone recites a *mani*, a four-line folk verse, and the verse is taken as the fortune of the object's owner.

The festival is not only Turkish. In the old Julian calendar, 6 May falls on 23 April, St George's Day, and spring feasts on that day are kept across the Balkans; the Roma of the Balkans and Thrace know it as Ederlezi. In 2017 UNESCO inscribed *Spring celebration, Hıdrellez* on its list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity, as a joint file of Turkey and North Macedonia. And in the legend of Kırkpınar ([unit 5](a2-u05-culture)) as Turkey's Ministry of Culture tells it, the brothers Ali and Selim fought their famous bout, which lasted through the night, on a Hıdırellez day.
Here is a Hıdırellez night in the Turkish of this unit:

blocks.tr: Bu gece Hıdırellez! Hadi, bahçeye çıkalım ve dilek dileyelim. Ben kâğıda küçük bir ev çizeyim. Sen ne çizeceksin? Dileklerimizi gülün dallarına asalım. Hızır bu gece bize de gelsin, dileklerimiz gerçek olsun!
blocks.en: Tonight is Hıdırellez! Come on, let's go out into the garden and make our wishes. I'll draw a little house on a piece of paper. What will you draw? Let's hang our wishes on the branches of the rose bush. May Hızır come to us too tonight, and may our wishes come true!

questions.q: What do people hang on rose bushes on Hıdırellez night?

questions.explain: *Ben kâğıda küçük bir ev çizeyim*: **I'll draw a little house on a piece of paper**.

sources.title: Spring celebration, Hıdrellez
sources.note: Inscribed in 2017 on the Representative List, a joint file of North Macedonia and Türkiye; held on 6 May; Hıdır and İlyas as protectors of earth and water and helpers of people in need; rituals for the wellbeing, fertility and prosperity of families, livestock and crops

sources.title: Hıdırellez
sources.note: Celebrated on 6 May, in some regions on 5 May; the meeting of Hızır and İlyas; the folk calendar of 186 Hızır days (6 May to 8 November) and 179 days of November; houses cleaned; lamb; outings to green places near water; the fortune game with objects in a pot left under a rose tree and drawn out with folk verses

sources.title: Hidrellez Traditions
sources.note: 6 May in the Gregorian calendar, 23 April in the Julian; Hızır drank the water of life, wanders among people in spring and helps those in difficulty, a symbol of spring and new life; houses cleaned, new clothes bought; small models of the house or garden wished for; the jar of rings and earrings under a rose tree

sources.title: Hıdırellez
sources.note: Night of 5 May and day of 6 May; 23 April Julian, St George's Day; Ederlezi; wishes on paper under rose trees; jumping over a fire three times; the pot of rings and earrings drawn out with mani verses

sources.title: Hıdırellez 2026 tarihi: Hıdırellez nedir, ne zaman kutlanacak?
sources.note: The night linking 5 and 6 May; wishes drawn or modelled, hung on or buried under a rose tree, collected in the morning and given to running water; the fire jumped three times; a coin under the rose tree kept as bereket parası

sources.title: Kırkpınar Wrestling
sources.note: In the legend, the brothers Ali and Selim wrestle again on a Hidrellez day, the festival of 6 May, through the day and into the night
